ARTICLE PREMIER. GENERALITES 
Dans le cadre du renforcement et du développement des équipements dédiés à la recherche scientifique 
au sein de l’Université de Mayotte, il est prévu d’acquérir un drone équipé d’un capteur bathymétrique 
de haute précision. Cet équipement viendra compléter les instruments de mesure déjà opérationnels et 
contribuera à élargir significativement les capacités d’étude, de surveillance et d’observation des milieux 
marins. 
L’intégration de cette technologie de bathymétrie permettra la réalisation de relevés détaillés des fonds 
marins ainsi que la production de modèles 3D précis de la topographie sous -marine. Ce nouvel outil 
constituera un apport déterminant pour les travaux de recherche, les missions de suivi environnemental 
et le développement de projets scientifiques innovants portés par l’université. 
Ces équipements renforceront la position de l’Université de Mayotte en tant qu’acteur régional majeur 
de la recherche scientifique, tout en affirmant son engagement en faveur de la préservation de 
l’environnement et de l’étude approfondie des écosystèmes de l’océan Indien. 
 
ARTICLE 2. OBJET DE LA CONSULTATION 
 
Le présent marché porte sur la fourniture d ’une solution complète, intégrée et opérationnelle de 
bathymétrie LiDAR aéroportée par drone. Le titulaire garantit la compatibilité et l’intégration 
fonctionnelle de l’ensemble des composants proposés, notamment le drone, le capteur bathymétrique, 
le système GNSS/INS, le système de fixation et d ’intégration, les accessoires, les logiciels nécessaires à 
l’acquisition et au traitement des données, ainsi que leur mise en service. 
2.1. Nature des prestations  
Les prestations objet du présent marché concernent : 
• La fourniture et le montage d’un drone destinés à l’activité de recherches scientifiques ;  
• La fourniture et le montage des équipements accessoires de fonctionnement et d’opération du 
drone ;   
• La fourniture et le montage d’un capteur bathymétrique ; 
• L’acquisition d’un logiciel de traitement des données compatible avec les 2 équipements ;  
• La formation et l’assistance à l’utilisation du capteur bathymétrique et des logiciels associés ; 
• Le transport des équipements y compris déconditionnement, démarches administratives 
associées et livraison à l ’Université de Mayotte (à l ’adresse indiquée dans les documents 
contractuels).

françaises et européennes en vigueur et tiendront compte, notamment des normes relatives à la 
réglementation, visant à garantir la sécurité,  la protection des données et la préservation de

L’équipement doit être compatible avec les usages suivants : 
• Surveillance environnementale ; 
• Acquisition de données topographiques et génération de modèles 3D ; 
• Cartographie bathymétrique ; 
• Réalisation de mesures géospatiales de haute précision. 
Le système doit permettre la collecte de données fiables, précises et exploitables afin de répondre aux 
exigences scientifiques de caractérisation, de suivi et de gestion des écosystèmes naturels. 
4.1.2. Caractéristiques techniques 
Le drone recherché doit présenter des performances techniques compatibles avec des missions 
professionnelles de recherche scientifique, en garantissant une fiabilité optimale, une stabilité de vol 
élevée et une capacité d’opération dans d es environnements variés, y compris en conditions 
météorologiques difficiles. Les spécifications ci-dessous définissent les exigences minimales auxquelles 
l’équipement devra répondre. 
• Autonomie : 
Le drone doit garantir une autonomie minimale de 30 minutes à vide et d’au moins 15 minutes avec 
la charge utile maximale. 
• Charge utile : 
Le drone doit être capable d’emporter une charge utile minimale de 5 kg, sans dégradation des 
performances essentielles de vol. 
• Vitesse maximale : 
Le drone doit pouvoir atteindre  une vitesse maximale d’au moins 1 5 m/s, dans des conditions 
opérationnelles standard. 
• Altitude de vol : 
Le drone doit être conforme aux altitudes maximales autorisées par la réglementation en vigueur 
pour les opérations professionnelles (scénarios DGAC ou normes européennes applicables).

• Systèmes de sécurité : 
Le drone doit intégrer des dispositifs de redondance pour les systèmes critiques (batterie de secours, 
GNSS/GPS, liaison de communication), ainsi qu’une fonction de retour automatique en cas de perte 
de signal, de défaillance critique ou de batterie faible. 
4.1.3. Fonctionnalités de navigation  
Le drone doit intégrer des fonctionnalités de navigation avancées, garantissant une précision élevée, 
une automatisation fiable des missions et une portée opérationnelle adaptée aux besoins de la re-
cherche scientifique. Les éléments ci-après définissent les exigences minimales attendues pour assurer 
la sécurité et l’efficacité des opérations aériennes. 
• Précision de positionnement : 
Le système de navigation doit permettre un positionnement précis avec une exactitude mini-
male de 0,3 m en 3D FIX et 0,03 m avec correction RTK. 
• Pilotage automatique : 
Le drone doit être équipé d’un système de pilotage automatique complet, incluant la planifica-
tion de missions par waypoints, la gestion des trajectoires préprogrammées et la fonctionnalité 
de retour automatique à la base (RTH) en cas d’incident ou de fin de mission. 
• Portée de communication :  
La radiocommande doit offrir une portée opérationnelle d’au moins 8 km, garantissant un 
contrôle stable et continu dans les zones d’intervention prévues. La portée annoncée devra être 
conforme à la réglementation européenne applicable aux opérations professionnelles en vi-
gueur au moment de l’exécution du marché.

opérationnelle immédiate, une autonomie prolongée et une maintenance courante facilitée. Les 
équipements complémentaires listés ci -dessous constituent le minimum requis pour  assurer la

Introduction 

FuturEnergy Ireland is a leading Irish wind developer established in 2021 as a stand-alone joint venture between Coillte and ESB. The company was formed with an aim to maximise the potential of Ireland’s unique wind and land resources and accelerate Ireland’s transformation to a low carbon energy economy.  FuturEnergy Ireland is targeting the development of 1GW of renewable energy by 2030 through the advancement of high-quality onshore wind and battery storage projects. These projects would power an estimated 730,000 homes annually, make a significant contribution to Ireland’s commitment to produce 80% of electricity from renewable sources by the end of this decade, and deliver material emissions reductions.  


Contract for service – Invitation to tender

(a) Introduction
FuturEnergy Ireland is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced panel of Contractors to undertake LiDAR topographical survey services as required. The survey is
intended to provide accurate and reliable terrain, surface, imagery and survey-control data to support project development, design and related technical activities.
The successful Contractors will be responsible for all necessary planning, permissions, survey control, data acquisition, processing, independent validation, reporting and final deliverables.
Candidates should note that the objective of this tender competition is twofold: A) to appoint successful firms to the panel, and B) to award an initial assignment which relates to Project 1 located in Co Laois detailed in Appendix 5 of this document. 
Tenderers should note that four further projects are expected to be awarded through the panel shortly after it is established. These projects are not exhaustive, and additional projects will be awarded through the panel during its term, subject to project requirements and the Contracting Entity’s discretion.

(b) Objectives
The appointed Contractors shall:
Undertake a complete LiDAR high-resolution aerial imagery survey of the specified survey area.
Establish robust survey control and independent validation checkpoints using survey-grade GNSS RTK/PPK methods.
Provide accurate, quality-assured terrain, surface, point-cloud, imagery, contour and survey-control deliverables in the formats specified.
Demonstrate compliance with the required coordinate reference system, accuracy, point-density, validation and reporting requirements.

(c) Scope of Services




1. Survey Planning, Permissions and Mobilisation
The Contractors shall prepare the survey methodology and flight plan, secure all necessary permissions and approvals, coordinate access requirements, identify constraints and confirm the proposed survey programme before mobilisation.

2. Survey Control and Referencing
The survey shall be referenced to the Irish Transverse Mercator (ITM) coordinate system and Malin Head Ordnance Datum (MHOD). Ground control and independent validation checkpoints shall be established using survey-grade GNSS RTK/PPK methods.
A minimum of 20% of survey control points shall be retained as independent checkpoints and shall not be used during processing.


3. LiDAR and Aerial Imagery Acquisition
The Contractors shall acquire LiDAR and high-resolution aerial imagery sufficient to generate accurate Digital Terrain Models, Digital Surface Models, classified point clouds and orthorectified imagery.
The LiDAR system shall provide a minimum of five returns per pulse and shall be capable of reliable ground penetration through dense vegetation and forestry cover.

4. Minimum Technical Requirements
Horizontal accuracy: hard detail, including buildings, walls, roads and other defined features, shall be <= +/-50 mm; soft detail, including vegetation and natural terrain features, shall be <= +/-75 mm.
Vertical accuracy: hard detail and open ground shall be <= +/-75 mm; vegetated and forested areas shall be <= +/-100 mm.
Point density: minimum average LiDAR density of 150 points/m2 and minimum classified ground density of 15 points/m2 beneath forest canopy.
All reported accuracies shall be verified using independent checkpoints not used during processing.

5. Processing, Classification and Quality Assurance
The Contractors shall process, classify and validate the survey data, document the processing workflow, undertake appropriate quality assurance and quality control, and report achieved point density and horizontal and vertical accuracy.

6. Required Deliverables
Raw and classified LiDAR point clouds in LAS/LAZ format.
Digital Terrain Model (DTM) GeoTIFF at 0.25 m resolution.
Digital Surface Model (DSM) GeoTIFF at 0.25 m resolution.
Canopy Height Model (CHM) GeoTIFF at 0.5 m resolution
Orthorectified RGB imagery with a ground sampling distance of 5 cm/pixel or better.
0.5 m contour dataset in ESRI Shapefile and AutoCAD DWG formats. (Optional)
Survey control coordinates and validation results.
Final survey report detailing the survey methodology, equipment, processing workflow, point density, and horizontal and vertical accuracy assessment.




7. Optional Project Photography and Videography
The Contractors may be requested to carry out occasional aerial photography and videography surveys to capture site imagery for communications, publicity, stakeholder engagement, reporting and promotional purposes. All outputs shall be provided in high-resolution digital formats suitable for print and online use.

Introduction 

FuturEnergy Ireland is a leading Irish wind developer established in 2021 as a stand-alone joint venture between Coillte and ESB. The company was formed with an aim to maximise the potential of Ireland’s unique wind and land resources and accelerate Ireland’s transformation to a low carbon energy economy.  FuturEnergy Ireland is targeting the development of 1GW of renewable energy by 2030 through the advancement of high-quality onshore wind and battery storage projects. These projects would power an estimated 730,000 homes annually, make a significant contribution to Ireland’s commitment to produce 80% of electricity from renewable sources by the end of this decade, and deliver material emissions reductions.  


Contract for service – Invitation to tender

(a) Introduction
FuturEnergy Ireland is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced panel of Contractors to undertake LiDAR topographical survey services as required. The survey is
intended to provide accurate and reliable terrain, surface, imagery and survey-control data to support project development, design and related technical activities.
The successful Contractors will be responsible for all necessary planning, permissions, survey control, data acquisition, processing, independent validation, reporting and final deliverables.
Candidates should note that the objective of this tender competition is twofold: A) to appoint successful firms to the panel, and B) to award an initial assignment which relates to Project 1 located in Co Laois detailed in Appendix 5 of this document. 
Tenderers should note that four further projects are expected to be awarded through the panel shortly after it is established. These projects are not exhaustive, and additional projects will be awarded through the panel during its term, subject to project requirements and the Contracting Entity’s discretion.

(b) Objectives
The appointed Contractors shall:
Undertake a complete LiDAR high-resolution aerial imagery survey of the specified survey area.
Establish robust survey control and independent validation checkpoints using survey-grade GNSS RTK/PPK methods.
Provide accurate, quality-assured terrain, surface, point-cloud, imagery, contour and survey-control deliverables in the formats specified.
Demonstrate compliance with the required coordinate reference system, accuracy, point-density, validation and reporting requirements.

(c) Scope of Services




1. Survey Planning, Permissions and Mobilisation
The Contractors shall prepare the survey methodology and flight plan, secure all necessary permissions and approvals, coordinate access requirements, identify constraints and confirm the proposed survey programme before mobilisation.

2. Survey Control and Referencing
The survey shall be referenced to the Irish Transverse Mercator (ITM) coordinate system and Malin Head Ordnance Datum (MHOD). Ground control and independent validation checkpoints shall be established using survey-grade GNSS RTK/PPK methods.
A minimum of 20% of survey control points shall be retained as independent checkpoints and shall not be used during processing.


3. LiDAR and Aerial Imagery Acquisition
The Contractors shall acquire LiDAR and high-resolution aerial imagery sufficient to generate accurate Digital Terrain Models, Digital Surface Models, classified point clouds and orthorectified imagery.
The LiDAR system shall provide a minimum of five returns per pulse and shall be capable of reliable ground penetration through dense vegetation and forestry cover.

4. Minimum Technical Requirements
Horizontal accuracy: hard detail, including buildings, walls, roads and other defined features, shall be <= +/-50 mm; soft detail, including vegetation and natural terrain features, shall be <= +/-75 mm.
Vertical accuracy: hard detail and open ground shall be <= +/-75 mm; vegetated and forested areas shall be <= +/-100 mm.
Point density: minimum average LiDAR density of 150 points/m2 and minimum classified ground density of 15 points/m2 beneath forest canopy.
All reported accuracies shall be verified using independent checkpoints not used during processing.

5. Processing, Classification and Quality Assurance
The Contractors shall process, classify and validate the survey data, document the processing workflow, undertake appropriate quality assurance and quality control, and report achieved point density and horizontal and vertical accuracy.

6. Required Deliverables
Raw and classified LiDAR point clouds in LAS/LAZ format.
Digital Terrain Model (DTM) GeoTIFF at 0.25 m resolution.
Digital Surface Model (DSM) GeoTIFF at 0.25 m resolution.
Canopy Height Model (CHM) GeoTIFF at 0.5 m resolution
Orthorectified RGB imagery with a ground sampling distance of 5 cm/pixel or better.
0.5 m contour dataset in ESRI Shapefile and AutoCAD DWG formats. (Optional)
Survey control coordinates and validation results.
Final survey report detailing the survey methodology, equipment, processing workflow, point density, and horizontal and vertical accuracy assessment.




7. Optional Project Photography and Videography
The Contractors may be requested to carry out occasional aerial photography and videography surveys to capture site imagery for communications, publicity, stakeholder engagement, reporting and promotional purposes. All outputs shall be provided in high-resolution digital formats suitable for print and online use.

normalized.description: IMPACT 10 is an ESA Earth Observation activity aimed at assessing and demonstrating the scientific and socio economic value generated by selected activities of the Earth and Mission Science Division (EOP SM). It focuses on scientific studies, mission science contributions, and programme enabling work supporting future EO missions. It also covers a new branch of "Future Science" activities. Within EOP SM, "Future Science" refers to forward looking science studies aligned with the ESA EO Science Strategy. These studies are designed to address fundamental Earth system science gaps that are not covered by current or planned missions. They therefore go beyond the scope of existing Science Plans activities. The activity will develop a robust and traceable methodology to assess both science impact and socio economic impact. Science impact will include, for example, scientific outputs, modelling advances, retrieval improvements, uncertainty characterisation, mission requirement support, community building, and uptake in international assessments. Socio economic impact will include, for example, industrial competitiveness, innovation spillovers, policy support, and broader societal and economic value.

normalized.title: TALLINN HELSINKI OPTICAL RELAY (THOR) TESTBED (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.092) - REQUESTED
normalized.description: The objective of the activity is to define and develop a free space optical communication testbed suitable for testing a cross-atmospheric optical connectivity in the horizontal link between Tallinn and Helsinki. Targeted Improvements: To create a terrestrial testbed capability allowing for demonstration and long-term communication testing. The testbed will provide information on the long-distance atmospheric channel and the stability of the optical links in fixed and mobile configuration. The testbed facility will support new technology developments for optical and quantum satellite communication. Description: Most of satellite constellations developed these days include intersatellite links. However, the adaptation of cross-atmospheric links remains to be progressing slowly. One of the challenges is the limited availability of outdoor, free-space testbeds. The proposed testbed facility will enable testing over the long-distance, cross-atmospheric channel created between two stations located in Tallinn and Helsinki. The testbed will allow for fixed-points free-space optical connection, demonstrating and validating a continuous datalink between interoperable terminals and transceivers aligned with satellite optical communication standards. The testbed should allow to collect and analyse information on the atmospheric channel over multiple seasons. It should monitor weather conditions and investigate beam dissipation dynamics and various mitigation strategies. The spatially dynamic optical links will also be demonstrated to test and validate a free-space optical datalink between moving terminals. The testbed should foresee and facilitate testing of quantum-encrypted free-space optical communication capabilities. The preparation to demonstrate data-relay with a satellite link is planned to be included in the activity.

normalized.description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity.  In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1]  1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.
